Pass each module quiz (70% or more). You can retry as often as you like.
Complete the three-month plan and the final assessment.

faq.q: Will this get me to number one on a search engine?
faq.a: No course can promise that. It teaches the methods that improve your chances honestly and how to measure the results.

faq.q: Do I need a website to practise?
faq.a: No. The labs use a sample business, and the practical tasks suggest auditing any small site you know.

faq.q: Is the content up to date?
faq.a: It focuses on principles that last. Search engines change details often, so the course points you to official guidance.

activities.title: Write a title and description
activities.objective: Write a page title and meta description that match the topic and invite a click.
activities.scenario: A home bakery in Pune sells eggless birthday cakes and wants to rank for 'eggless birthday cake in Pune'. Write the title and the description for its page.
steps: Write a line starting with Title: using the main phrase.
Write a line starting with Description: of one or two sentences.
Keep the title under 60 characters (about 10 words) and the description under 160 characters.
Mention a benefit and end the description with a call to action.

checks.label: A title line
checks.hint: Start the line with Title:.
checks.explain: The title is the clickable headline in search results.

checks.label: A description line
checks.hint: Start the line with Description:.
checks.explain: The description is the short text below the title.

checks.label: The main phrase appears
checks.hint: Include eggless birthday cake and Pune.
checks.explain: Telling the engine what the page is about helps it match searches.

checks.label: The place is mentioned
checks.hint: Include Pune.

checks.label: A call to action
checks.hint: End with something like Order today.
checks.explain: A clear next step raises clicks.

checks.label: Short enough to display
checks.hint: Keep it under 45 words in total.
checks.explain: Search results cut long titles and descriptions.

activities.title: Outline a page that deserves to rank
activities.objective: Structure a helpful page with a single H1 and clear subheadings.
activities.scenario: Plan a guide called 'How to choose a school bag for a child'. Write the outline with headings and a short opening paragraph.
steps: Add one Heading 1 with the guide's title.
Write an opening paragraph of two or three sentences that answers the main question.
Add at least four Heading 2 sections (for example size, weight, straps, material).
Add a short list of checks under one of the sections.

checks.label: One main heading
checks.hint: Use Heading 1 once.
checks.explain: A single clear H1 tells readers and engines the topic.

checks.label: Four or more subheadings
checks.hint: Use Heading 2 for each section.
checks.explain: Subheadings make a page scannable and cover subtopics.

checks.label: An opening paragraph that answers the question
checks.hint: Write at least two full sentences.

checks.label: A short checklist
checks.hint: Use the bullet button.
checks.explain: Lists are easy to read and often shown in results.

checks.label: The topic phrase appears
checks.hint: Include school bag.
checks.explain: The page should clearly be about the topic.

checks.label: Between 80 and 300 words
checks.hint: Enough to be useful, short enough to outline.
checks.explain: Depth matters, but this is an outline.

activities.title: Prioritise keywords
activities.objective: Score keywords by opportunity so you can target the best ones first.
activities.scenario: A bakery has researched five phrases. Opportunity is monthly searches times the chance of winning, divided by difficulty.
steps: In E2 enter =B2*C2/D2 for opportunity, and fill down to E6.
In B8 find the highest opportunity with MAX.
In B9 count how many phrases have more than 500 searches using COUNTIF.
In B10 show the phrase with the top score using IF on the first and second rows only: IF(E2=B8,A2,A3) is enough for a model answer.
Make the heading A1 bold.

checks.label: E2 is the opportunity score
checks.explain: More searches and a better chance raise it; difficulty lowers it.

checks.label: E6 is filled
checks.hint: Fill the formula down to row 6.
checks.explain: The same rule applies to every keyword.

checks.label: B8 is the highest score
checks.hint: =MAX(E2:E6)

checks.label: B9 counts phrases over 500 searches
checks.hint: =COUNTIF(B2:B6,">500")
checks.explain: COUNTIF counts the rows that meet a condition.

checks.label: B10 shows the top phrase
checks.explain: IF compares each score with the maximum.

checks.label: Heading A1 is bold
checks.hint: Click A1 and press the bold button.
checks.explain: Bold headings separate labels from data.

activities.title: Read the search report
activities.objective: Work out click-through rate and spot pages with potential.
activities.scenario: A search console report shows five pages. Compute each page's click-through rate and find the ones worth improving.
steps: In E2 enter clicks divided by impressions, fill down to E6.
In F2 write IF(AND(D2>=4,D2<=10,E2<0.03),"Improve","OK") and fill down.
In B8 total the clicks and in B9 count the pages marked Improve using COUNTIF.
Create a bar chart of clicks by page.

checks.label: E2 is the click-through rate
checks.explain: CTR shows how often the result was clicked.

checks.label: F2 flags page 1
checks.explain: Pages on page one with a low CTR need a better title.

checks.label: F4 flags page 3
checks.hint: Fill the formula down.
checks.explain: The same rule applies to every page.

checks.label: B8 totals the clicks
checks.hint: =SUM(C2:C6)

checks.label: B9 counts pages to improve
checks.hint: =COUNTIF(F2:F6,"Improve")

checks.label: A bar chart of clicks
checks.hint: Chart type bar with labels A2:A6 and values C2:C6.
checks.explain: A chart shows which pages bring visitors.

activities.title: Write a short SEO audit
activities.objective: Report findings in priority order so an owner knows what to fix first.
activities.scenario: You audited a small furniture shop's website. Write the summary for the owner.
steps: Add headings: Summary, Findings, Priorities.
Under Findings, list at least four problems (for example slow images, missing titles, broken links, thin pages).
Under Priorities, write a numbered list of actions in order, most valuable first.
Keep the report between 100 and 300 words.

checks.label: Three headings
checks.hint: Use Heading 2 for Summary, Findings and Priorities.
checks.explain: A clear structure helps the owner decide.

checks.label: Sections in order
checks.hint: Summary, Findings, Priorities.
checks.explain: Start with the overview and end with action.

checks.label: At least four findings in a bullet list
checks.hint: Use the bullet button.
checks.explain: Specific findings are easier to act on.

checks.label: A numbered list of priorities
checks.hint: Use the numbered list button.
checks.explain: Numbers show the order of importance.

checks.label: Mentions titles or speed
checks.hint: Mention titles, speed or links in your report.

spec.what: an SEO term such as title or speed

checks.label: Between 100 and 300 words
checks.hint: Concise but complete.

activities.title: Final project: build a 3-month SEO plan
activities.objective: Estimate traffic and value from improving rankings, and choose which pages to start with.
activities.scenario: Five pages could be improved. Estimate extra monthly visits from moving up, then the value of those visits.
steps: In D2 compute extra visits: searches times the new click rate minus the old click rate (E2 minus C2 pattern: B2*(D2-C2) is not correct here; use the columns as labelled).
In F2 enter extra visits = B2*(E2-D2) and fill to F6.
In G2 enter value = F2*$B$9 (value per visit) and fill to G6.
In F8 and G8 total extra visits and value.
In B11 show the page with the most extra value using INDEX-free logic: use IF(G2=MAX(G2:G6),A2,...) for the first two rows.
Chart the extra visits by page.

checks.label: F2 is extra visits for page 1
checks.explain: More clicks from the same searches.

checks.label: F5 is filled
checks.hint: Fill down to row 6.
checks.explain: The same rule applies to each page.

checks.label: G2 is the value of those visits
checks.explain: Lock the value-per-visit cell with dollar signs.

checks.label: F8 totals the extra visits
checks.hint: =SUM(F2:F6)

checks.label: G8 totals the value
checks.hint: =SUM(G2:G6)

checks.label: B11 names the starting page
checks.hint: =IF(G2=MAX(G2:G6),A2,A5)
checks.explain: Pick the page with the most extra value; here the first or the fourth leads.

checks.label: A bar chart of extra visits
checks.hint: Chart type bar with labels A2:A6 and values F2:F6.
